subject: math

entries: Riemann sums: slicing area under a curve: four wide rectangles under y = x^2 from 0 to 2 estimate 3.75, eight narrow ones tighten it to 3.1875, and the limit of the sums is the exact area 8/3.
slots.label: Riemann sums: slicing area
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Signed area: below the axis counts negative: the triangle above the axis contributes +2 and the triangle below contributes -0.5, so the integral of x from -1 to 2 is the net signed area 3/2.
slots.label: Signed area: below the axis
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: u-substitution: the chain rule in reverse: setting u = x^2 turns 2x dx into du, so the integral of 2x e^(x^2) from 0 to 1 becomes the integral of e^u from 0 to 1, which is e - 1.
slots.label: u-substitution: the chain rule in reverse
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Volumes of revolution: stacking discs: each slice of the rotated solid is a disc of radius x^2 and thickness dx, and stacking them gives V = pi times the integral of x^4 from 0 to 1 = pi/5.
slots.label: Volumes of revolution: stacking discs
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The +C trap: only for indefinite integrals: the antiderivative x^3/3 evaluated from 1 to 2 gives 8/3 - 1/3, and any +C would appear at both limits and cancel, leaving 7/3.
slots.label: The +C trap
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The limit of Riemann sums over a fixed interval [a, b], equal to net signed area and written as a single number such as 7/3 - it never carries a +C.
slots.label: Definite integral
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The family of all antiderivatives of a function, written with +C because differentiating any constant gives zero: the integral of x^2 is x^3/3 + C.
slots.label: Indefinite integral
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An estimate of the area under a curve made by slicing the interval into rectangles and adding width times height; under y = x^2 from 0 to 2, n = 4 gives 3.75 and the limit is 8/3.
slots.label: Riemann sum
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Area counted positive above the x-axis and negative below it: for y = x from -1 to 2 the triangles give 2 - 0.5 = 3/2.
slots.label: Signed area
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The chain rule in reverse: set u equal to an inner function so its derivative absorbs the remaining factors, as u = x^2 turns the integral of 2x e^(x^2) into the integral of e^u.
slots.label: U-substitution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The volume swept when a curve rotates about an axis, built by stacking discs: V = pi times the integral of r^2 dx, which for y = x^2 from 0 to 1 gives pi/5.
slots.label: Volume of revolution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 integration: Riemann sums, u-substitution, volumes of revolution
